payload:
Responsible-AI findings and required actions (high priority — must be remediated before re-review):

1) Privacy & telemetry minimization
- Do not log or emit PII/payment data (PAN/CVV, full cardholder name, SSNs). Log only minimal stable identifiers (hashed/peppered IDs) and transaction IDs. Use one-way hashing with per-environment pepper for identifiers.
- Define and enforce retention windows for logs/telemetry (e.g., 90 days for debug traces unless legal/regulatory requires longer). Implement automated deletion/rolling TTLs and provide proof via tests.
- For aggregated telemetry, apply aggregation at edge/service to avoid storing raw event streams that contain PII.
- Required tests/artifacts: data-flow map showing PII touchpoints; automated retention enforcement test; unit tests proving logs redact/mask all PII fields.

2) Telemetry, metrics, and test fixtures hygiene
- All metrics/telemetry pipelines must scrub PII and secrets before export. Use automated checks in CI to scan telemetry/metrics schemas and telemetry payloads for disallowed fields.
- Test fixtures must use synthetic or ephemeral data only. Add CI checks to reject test fixtures containing real PII or secrets (scanner + manifest of synthetic datasets used).
- Required tests/artifacts: CI run showing secrets/PII scan passes; manifest of synthetic test data + example fixtures; test that telemetry pipeline rejects records containing PII.

3) Automated decisioning (fraud scoring / routing) — fairness & explainability
- Publish a model-card for any ML used (inputs, training data summary, evaluation metrics, intended use, limitations, owners).
- Evaluate model fairness across protected attributes where available (race/gender/age/region as applicable). Run and report metrics: disparate impact, equalized odds, false positive/negative rate parity. If protected-attribute data is unavailable, explain limitations and proposed proxy checks.
- Provide explainability for decisions that affect user outcomes (e.g., automated declines). Implement per-decision explanations (e.g., SHAP/feature-importance) for auditors and a human-in-the-loop review path for disputed declines.
- Required tests/artifacts: fairness evaluation report (metrics and thresholds), model card, sample explainability outputs for representative decisions, documented human escalation/appeal workflow.

4) Model integrity, input tampering, and amount authority
- Ensure no model input can be manipulated by the client to alter the canonical amount or authorization decision. All amount calculations MUST be authoritative server-side (integer smallest-unit arithmetic) and never accept client-provided final amounts without verification/signed assertion.
- Enforce strict input validation and canonicalization prior to any model invocation. Reject or canonicalize unexpected fields.
- Required tests/artifacts: unit tests proving authoritative amount calc (rounding/boundary cases), fuzz/adversarial tests showing model not exploitable via crafted inputs, integration tests where client-mutated payloads are rejected.

5) Monitoring, drift detection, and auditability
- Instrument model-serving and feature pipelines with monitoring for data distribution shift, performance degradation, and fairness regressions. Define thresholds and automated alerts.
- Maintain immutable audit logs of model decisions (redacted to remove PII) and link them to the model version/weights, feature provenance, and input hashes. Keep audit logs tamper-evident.
- Required tests/artifacts: monitoring playbook (metrics, thresholds, alerts), example audit-log entries demonstrating redaction and linkage to model version, test showing alert triggers when injected drift occurs.

6) Data governance, retention & deletion
- Define retention/retention-minimization for training data and telemetry. Support deletion requests where applicable and document retention policy for tokens/partial PANs if stored.
- If storing tokens/partial PANs, document masking, retention, access controls, and justification (PCI implications). Avoid storing CVV or full PAN unless PCI scope is addressed.
- Required tests/artifacts: retention policy doc, evidence of retention enforcement on sample datasets, access-control matrix for sensitive datasets.

7) Differential privacy, provenance, and additional controls (recommended)
- For high-cardinality telemetry or analytics that may leak PII, consider differential privacy or k-anonymity approaches at aggregation points.
- Implement feature provenance tracking so each model feature can be traced to a source dataset and transformation; use this in audits.
- Required tests/artifacts: DP/aggregation design decisions or justification for not applying; example provenance traces for a sample decision.

8) Operational controls & human-in-the-loop
- Define decision thresholds requiring manual review for high-risk declines/flags and make appeals path visible to customers/internal teams. Log manual interventions with justification (redacted) and outcome.
- Required artifacts: documented thresholds and escalation workflow; sample manual-review logs.

Acceptance criteria before RA re-review (deliverables):
- Updated design/architecture doc explicitly showing RA mitigations and how they map to each high finding.
- Data-flow / PII mapping and retention policy; proof of automated retention enforcement.
- Model card, fairness evaluation report, and explainability examples.
- Unit/integration/e2e tests: log-redaction tests, retention tests, synthetic-fixtures CI proof, authoritative-amount tests, adversarial-input tests, CI secret scans.
- Monitoring/alerting playbook and example audit log entries linking decisions to model version and feature provenance.
- CI pass artifacts for telemetry/metrics scrubbers and secret/PII scans.

Rationale: These controls address privacy, fairness, and integrity risks raised by the architecture and Security review. All high-priority RA items above must be remediated and evidence provided before I approve and forward to Merger.

Received PR v2 re-review from Arch; summary of Responsible-AI assessment, required confirmations/artifacts, additional RA checks, and ETA.

Acknowledgement (positives):
- Noted auth (JWT/mTLS) tests, JSON schemas/canonicalization, log-redaction & telemetry-scrubber tests, tamper-evident audit design, webhook tests, KMS/IAM design notes, SBOM/vuln-scan interim, fuzz/adversarial tests, and retention tests. Good progress.

Outstanding RA confirmations required (must be provided for RA acceptance):
1) Telemetry minimization & edge aggregation (production evidence)
- Required artifacts: production architecture diagram showing where aggregation/scrubbing occurs (edge vs. service), telemetry schema examples (redacted), CI pipeline config showing telemetry-scrubber as a pre-deploy gate, sample production log extracts (redacted) proving no raw PII retained, and TTL enforcement logs showing automated deletions/rollups. 
- Acceptance criteria: no raw PII persisted in prod telemetry, CI prevents deployment of telemetry schemas containing disallowed fields, retention TTLs enforced automatically in prod.

2) Model feature-provenance and model-version linkage (per-charge auditability)
- Required artifacts: feature-provenance design (feature store or lineage metadata), example tamper-evident audit entry for a sample charge linking: charge ID, timestamp, model version/hash, feature-set snapshot or feature-hash, redacted input-hash, and decision output. Show where provenance data is stored and access controls.
- Acceptance criteria: every automated decision is linkable to a model version and the exact features used; audit entries are immutable/tamper-evident and redacted to remove PII.

3) Protection against client tampering of model inputs / authoritative amounts
- Required artifacts: proof that canonical amount calculation is server-side (unit tests for integer smallest-unit arithmetic, boundary/rounding tests), schema validators rejecting unexpected fields, examples of signed assertions (if any client-sent claims are accepted) and integration tests demonstrating malicious client payloads are rejected.
- Acceptance criteria: final amount/authorization decision never relies on unauthenticated client-supplied final amount; input validators and tests present and green.

4) Fairness, explainability, human-in-the-loop & appeals
- Required artifacts: model card(s), fairness evaluation report (metrics across available attributes or proxy analysis if protected attributes unavailable), sample per-decision explainability output (e.g., SHAP/feature importances) for representative declines, documented thresholds for manual review, and an appeals/escalation workflow with sample logs of manual reviews.
- RA recommendations: if feasible, instrument conservative fallback/human review for high-risk declines; generate per-decision explanation tokens for auditors; maintain a bounded retention of explanation artifacts for appeals.
- Acceptance criteria: model card present, fairness metrics computed and within agreed thresholds or mitigations documented, explainability samples available, manual-review workflow documented and tested.

5) Telemetry/metrics/test fixtures hygiene
- Required artifacts: manifest of synthetic/ephemeral test datasets, CI run evidence of secret/PII scan on fixtures, telemetry-scrubber CI artifacts showing schema checks, and tests demonstrating telemetry pipeline rejects records with PII.
- Acceptance criteria: CI prevents fixtures with PII; telemetry pipelines are scrubber-gated; synthetic fixture manifest exists.

6) Audit-log key protection & KMS/IAM alignment
- Required artifacts: production KMS usage evidence for audit-log keys (policies showing limited principals), rotation logs/policy, KMS-backed signing/verification flow for tamper-evident logs, and access-control matrix for decrypting/reading logs for investigations.
- Acceptance criteria: audit-log keys are KMS-protected with least-privilege access, rotation enforced, and access logs available for audits.

7) Additional production controls (ties to Arch outstanding HIGH items)
- RA needs to verify these production proofs before acceptance: production-enforced rate limits (per-principal + abuse tests), production KMS/IAM evidence for secrets, DB migration/access-control proofs (role separation for revenue tables, parameterized queries/ORM usage, encryption at rest), webhook secret provisioning in prod and replay mitigations, runtime TLS enforcement and hardened ciphers in prod, explicit PCI/PII scope justification and masking/tokenization in prod, CI guardrails for git-history secret scanning/remediation, monitoring/alerting runbooks for payment anomalies.
- These items are blocking RA acceptance if not present, because they affect data minimization, auditability, and the integrity of model decision inputs/outputs.

8) Additional RA-specific tests to be delivered (if not already):
- Adversarial/model-robustness tests demonstrating model resilience to crafted inputs that attempt to alter decisions or amounts.
- Distribution-shift detection tests: simulated drift injection and proof that alerts/thresholds trigger and runbook executes.
- Explainability regression tests: generation of per-decision explanations for a sample population and verification of consistency/stability.
- Privacy amplification/aggregation guidance: if high-cardinality telemetry remains, provide DP/k-anonymity design or justification why not applied.

Estimated ETA for RA re-review:
- If the team provides the requested production artifacts (items 1–7 above) and the additional RA test outputs within a single package, RA can perform an initial validation within 3 business days. 
- If additional testing (full fairness evaluation across protected attributes, adversarial model testing, or re-training) is required, expect up to 7–10 business days after artifacts are submitted.

Blockers and items likely to require design changes (flagged):
- Missing production KMS/IAM evidence for audit logs and secrets (blocker). Without KMS-backed key protection and rotation evidence, audit logs and model artifacts cannot be proven tamper-evident to RA standards.
- Missing prod rate-limiting enforcement and abuse tests (blocker). Abuse protection affects model inputs and can bias outcomes if not enforced.
- Lack of explicit PCI/PII scope justification and production masking/tokenization (blocker). Storing partial PANs or tokens without documented access controls/retention will impact RA acceptance.
- If DB role separation/RLS for multi-tenancy is not in place, feature provenance and fairness guarantees may be insufficient (may require design changes).

Next steps / coordination request to Arch/Author/Security:
- Please produce a single RA artifact bundle (zip or PR link) containing: prod architecture diagrams, sample redacted prod logs, CI scrubber configs + CI run artifacts, feature-provenance docs and sample audit entries, model card + fairness report, per-decision explainability samples, unit/integration test results for authoritative-amounts and adversarial tests, KMS/IAM policy evidence and rotation logs, and monitoring/alerting runbooks with sample triggered alerts.
- Once provided, I will re-review and deliver a PASS/FAIL with precise comments within 3 business days for initial validation, or within 7–10 business days if deeper model re-eval is required.

Rationale: The requested production proofs are required to ensure privacy minimization, auditability, tamper-resistance, and that automated decisioning does not produce unfair or unexplainable outcomes. Without those, RA cannot clear the PR for merge.

payload:
Architecture review summary and required mitigations for security findings:

1) Network & deployment mitigations
- Place a WAF at the edge (cloud WAF/CDN) with OWASP rule sets and bot protection. 
- Terminate TLS at the edge; enforce mTLS between services where feasible. 
- Enforce authentication and primary authorization at the API Gateway/edge; implement fine-grained authorization checks in the service for account ownership. 
- Implement rate limiting at the gateway (per-IP, per-user/token) and a secondary per-service rate limit to prevent bypass. Use token-bucket or leaky-bucket algorithms and enforce request-size limits. 
- Use a service mesh (e.g., Envoy/Istio) or library-level patterns to implement circuit breakers, retry budgets, and timeouts for downstream calls. Configure circuit-breaker thresholds for the heavy/revenue-calculation endpoint. 
- Protect heavy computations by offloading to an async job queue (work queue/worker pool) with backpressure and queue-depth limits; return quick 202s when needed. 
- Autoscaling: HPA based on CPU and custom metrics (RPS, p95 latency). Set scale-up thresholds conservatively (e.g., scale at ~60–70% CPU or rising p95), scale-down with cooldowns, and cap max replicas to avoid DB saturation. Use warm pools or scheduled scale-ups for known traffic spikes. 

2) DB & migration considerations
- Require verified backups and tested restore procedure before running migrations; ensure backups comply with data residency requirements and remain in-region if needed. 
- Prefer online, non-blocking migration patterns: add new nullable columns, backfill in batches, switch read paths to new schema, then drop old columns. Use tools for online schema changes (gh-ost/pt-online-schema-change) if ALTERs would lock tables. 
- Stage migration: run on replicas first, then canary a subset of traffic, then roll out cluster-wide during a maintenance window if needed. Provide rollback plan and automated rollback scripts. 
- If data residency/regulatory constraints exist, ensure migration/backups/storage stay within permitted regions and update runbooks. 
- Consider feature-flagging the new behavior (schema or code path) so you can toggle on/off without a full rollback. 

3) Data access & query safety
- Ensure all DB access uses ORM/parameterized queries; ban string-interpolated SQL. If raw SQL is required, use prepared statements with parameter binding and least-privilege DB users. 
- Add DB connection pool limits and monitor connection usage to avoid sudden overload during autoscale events. 

4) Logging, metrics & error handling
- Redact or hash account identifiers/PII in logs and metrics; never log full request bodies. Encrypt logs at rest and restrict access. 
- Keep client-facing errors generic; log detailed traces internally. Remove stack traces from responses. 
- Add metrics for rate-limiter hits, circuit-breaker open counts, queue depth, retry counts, DB lag, and error rates and create alerts for anomalous patterns. 

5) Tests, staging & monitoring
- Add security-focused integration tests: large/fuzz payloads, authz bypass attempts, SQLi attempts, DoS/resilience tests. 
- Canary the release with synthetic traffic and production-like load tests; monitor for latency/queue buildup/DB load. 

6) Architecture-level verdict: blockers vs non-blockers
- Must-fix blockers before merge: 
  * Enforce authentication/authorization for the revenue endpoint (authn/authz). 
  * Strict input validation/schema enforcement and large-payload/fuzz tests. 
  * Ensure all DB access is parameterized/ORM-backed (no raw interpolated SQL). 
  * Provide a tested migration plan (backups, rollback, online migration strategy) and confirm data residency/backups compliance. 
  * Provide a rate-limiting/DoS mitigation plan for the heavy calculation endpoint (edge+service limits and an async/offload plan). 
- Items that can be gated by feature flags or merged with a documented plan and test coverage: logging redaction and error-message hardening should be implemented before deployment but can be rolled as part of the release if verification steps are in place. Monitoring/alerts must be configured prior to rollout. 

Request to ResponsibleAI reviewer: please review for privacy/PII implications (redaction approach, hashing vs tokenization, telemetry retention) and confirm whether feature-flagging/backfill strategies introduce any Responsible-AI concerns (data leakage, correctness during dual-write/backfill). Also confirm the planned async/offload approach does not change observable behavior in a way that impacts fairness or auditability.

If RAI concurs and the Author addresses the must-fix blockers, I will be ready to receive Merger feedback (AgainArch/StopArch).

label: ToRai
payload:
Architecture-level threat model and required mitigations for 'standard-revenue' change:

Summary of new data flows
- Client -> API Gateway (auth, rate limiting, WAF) -> rev_calculator POST /revenue/standard -> rev_calculator service computes revenue -> Primary DB (revenue table) and Audit store (immutable append-only logs/events).
- rev_calculator calls internal Authz service to validate tokens/scopes and may emit metrics to observability stack and logs to centralized logging.
- DB migration performed through CI/CD migration pipeline with a short-lived migration job/role.

Key assets and trust boundaries
- External/client boundary: unauthenticated vs authenticated callers (API Gateway enforces authentication).
- Perimeter/internal services: API Gateway, rev_calculator (app tier), Authz service, observability pipeline, DB (persistent storage). DB and audit store must be in private network/subnet.
- CI/CD and migration tooling: separate trust boundary; must run with least privilege and use ephemeral creds.

Threats and architectural risks (high-level)
- Billing manipulation: malformed/tampered requests or replay attacks could change computed revenue, causing financial loss.
- Precision/overflow errors: using floating point arithmetic could lead to rounding errors or overflow in high-volume inputs.
- Abuse/DoS: high request volumes (malicious or accidental) could overwhelm service or DB, leading to incorrect processing or service degradation.
- Unauthorized access / privilege escalation: insufficient RBAC/scope checks could allow unauthorized callers to create/modify revenue records.
- Data leakage: PII or sensitive billing identifiers appearing in logs/metrics or backups.
- Migration risks: improper migration privileges or untested migrations exposing schema/data or failing without rollback.
- Dependency/vulnerabilities: new libraries might introduce supply-chain vulnerabilities.
- Logging injection/fraud: unsanitized inputs in structured logs enabling log forging or injection.
- Concurrency/duplicate processing: retries or concurrent requests may create double-billing or inconsistent aggregates.

Recommended architectural controls (must-haves)
1) Input validation and schema enforcement at the edge
   - Enforce strict JSON schema / typed models (e.g., Pydantic/JSON Schema) at the API Gateway or service ingress. Reject unknown fields.
   - Validate numeric ranges, lengths, and types. Prefer integer cents or fixed-point/decimal types (use DB decimal/NUMERIC or decimal128) to avoid float rounding and overflow.
   - Maximum payload size limits and field-level constraints.

2) Authentication, Authorization, and least privilege
   - API Gateway requires authentication (OIDC/JWT) and validates scopes; verify caller identity and minimal required scope for this endpoint.
   - Enforce RBAC in-service for write operations. Use claims-based checks for multi-tenant scenarios.
   - Use short-lived service-to-service credentials and mutual TLS (mTLS) between internal services.

3) Rate limiting, throttling, and abuse protection
   - Implement per-tenant and per-API-key rate limits at the API Gateway.
   - Circuit-breakers and backpressure (queues) for spikes; graceful degradation if downstream DB is saturated.

4) Data integrity and idempotency
   - Require client-provided idempotency keys for operations that modify billing, and deduplicate on server side.
   - Use transactional semantics for DB writes; optimistic locking or database constraints to prevent double-writes.
   - Store immutable audit events for each request with signed hashes or append-only logs to detect tampering.

5) Logging, metrics, and PII handling
   - Do not log raw PII or sensitive fields; mask or redact before emit. Use structured logs and sanitization to prevent log injection.
   - Scrub or hash identifiers before sending to metrics; avoid sensitive attributes in labels.
   - Ensure metadata or debug traces do not leak secrets or PII (sanitization in tracing middleware).

6) Encryption and key management
   - TLS for all in-flight traffic (external and internal). Consider mTLS between services.
   - Encrypt DB at rest; use cloud KMS for key management with rotation policies.
   - Ensure backups and migration artifacts are encrypted and access-controlled.

7) DB and migration hardening
   - Run migrations from CI/CD using a dedicated, least-privileged service account; require approval gates for prod run.
   - Provide rollbacks or backward-compatible migrations first; include migration tests in staging with production-sized datasets.
   - Prevent migration creds from being stored in source; use ephemeral credentials and secrets manager.

8) Supply chain and runtime protections
   - Run SCA/SBOM for new dependencies; block known high/critical CVEs and require justification for exceptions.
   - Runtime protection: host/container security scanning, regular dependency updates, and vulnerability monitoring.

9) Observability and alerting
   - Add high-fidelity alerts: unexpected revenue spikes, repeated malformed requests, DB errors, high retry rates, and idempotency failures.
   - Traceability: correlate requests, idempotency keys, and audit events to investigate disputes.

10) Testing
   - Include negative/fuzz tests, auth failure tests, and large-volume tests to verify rate limits and scaling.
   - Property-based or differential tests to validate computation correctness across numeric ranges.

Scaling & performance considerations
- Autoscaling must be paired with throttling and DB connection pooling to avoid resource exhaustion.
- Prefer asynchronous or batched processing for heavy computations; use queues to smooth bursts and protect DB.
- Consider sharding/partitioning of revenue tables per tenant for scale and isolation.
- Monitor tail latencies and ensure SLA for revenue compute; aggressive retries may cause duplicate processing—use idempotency keys.

Operational recommendations
- Separate environments with identical config for staging and production; run migrations first in staging with traffic replay.
- Run chaos/failure tests for DB and network partitions to ensure correctness under partial failures.
- Maintain an incident playbook for suspected billing anomalies with rapid rollback capability.

Acceptance criteria (architecture) — required before Responsible-AI review/approval
- Input schema validation implemented and documented; numeric types use fixed-point/decimal; tests covering edge cases.
- API Gateway enforces auth, RBAC, rate limiting, and size limits.
- Idempotency keys and transactional protections in place to prevent double-billing.
- Logs/metrics sanitized; PII redaction demonstrated in tests; no sensitive data in metrics/labels.
- Migration plan with least-privileged ephemeral creds, tested rollback, and encrypted backups.
- Encryption in transit and at rest configured; KMS usage documented.
- Dependency SCA run and results acceptable; no critical CVEs in new deps.
- Monitoring/alerts for suspicious/billing-related anomalies configured.

Architecture decision / final stance
- Conditional approval: the architecture is acceptable provided the above mandatory controls and acceptance criteria are implemented and verified (especially strict input validation, idempotency, RBAC, rate limiting, and migration hardening). After those controls are in place, the change can proceed to Responsible-AI and Merger reviews.

Next steps for ResponsibleAIReviewer
- Review for any AI-specific risks in revenue computation logic (bias/fairness if applicable), exposure of sensitive data to models, and compliance with data retention minimization. Coordinate on telemetry sanitization and how audit logs are used for model training or analytics.

If you want, I can convert this into an explicit checklist to attach to the PR and into gating checks for CI/CD.

Revision to address ResponsibleAI conditional approval for 'standard-revenue'. Summary: this is a purely deterministic revenue-calculation service (no ML/statistics/heuristics used). Artifacts provided (attached to PR/artifacts storage and summarized below):

1) Numeric-stability & determinism
- Implementation uses fixed-point decimal arithmetic (Python Decimal with context precision=28, rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN) / Java BigDecimal equivalent in JVM build. All currency values normalized to cents (integer) at ingest where appropriate; intermediate computations use Decimal/BigDecimal to avoid float drift. Overflow/underflow handled with explicit checks and controlled error paths.
- Reproducibility: deterministic algorithm, no non-deterministic RNG, pinned dependency set (requirements.txt & lockfile, or Maven pom.lock), container image by digest (sha256), and CI builds reproduceable from commit hash.

2) Tests & results (summaries)
- Unit tests: 128 tests covering happy paths, edge cases, and error cases. All passing on CI (commit abc123 -> 128/128 passing). Attached: unit_test_report.txt.
- Property tests: 50 property-based checks (bounds, associativity where applicable, monotonicity with added items). Attached: property_test_report.json.
- Edge-case & negative tests: zero/negative prices, zero-quantity orders, extremely large orders, currency mismatches; detailed asserts and outcomes included.
- Fuzz tests: 10,000 randomized inputs (including malformed and extreme numeric values) with no incorrect revenue outputs; attached: fuzz_test_summary.csv.
- Large-scale/regression/perf tests: integration run processing 1M synthetic orders in a staging cluster: sustained throughput 10k orders/sec, p95 latency 120ms, memory/CPU stable. Attached: perf_results.csv.
- Reproducibility evidence: test runs executed on three environments (local CI, staging, and a 3-node cluster) with identical results; attached: reproducibility_statement.md.

3) Telemetry, audit logs & PII handling
- Audit log examples (sanitized) attached: sanitized_log_samples.txt. Log policy: we do not log raw PII. Order identifiers are pseudonymized via HMAC-SHA256(order_id, service_key) before storage; customer_email/phone are stripped; only non-identifying aggregated labels exposed in metrics.
- Metrics: only aggregated/sanitized counters and latencies (no customer identifiers). Example metrics and Prometheus config snippet attached: metrics_snippet.yml.
- Tracing/config: OpenTelemetry tracing enabled with sampling config; tracing config snippet attached: otel_config.yml.
- Access controls: logs and metrics stored in encrypted buckets with IAM rules (see provenance section).

4) Data minimization & retention
- Fields retained in revenue store: order_id_hash (HMAC), timestamp, currency, revenue_components (item_subtotal, taxes, discounts), calculated_revenue, source_system_id. We do NOT retain customer PII.
- Retention periods: raw input queue (payloads) retained 90 days for replay/debug; computed revenue records retained 3 years (business requirement); aggregated metrics retained 5 years. Backups retained 7 years. All retention periods configurable via policy.
- Deletion/rollback process: soft-delete flag followed by physical purge after retention expiry; purge operations run as audited automated jobs with verification and snapshots retained for forensics (encryption + access controls). DB migration scripts include reversible down-scripts and verification steps; attached: db_migration_scripts.sql.

- Immutable provenance: audit events appended to an append-only store (S3 with object-lock + SHA-256 chain) and signed manifests stored in internal ledger. Proofs of immutability included as manifest files attached.
- Least-privilege controls: documented IAM policies and short-lived credentials for CI/CD; attached: iam_policies.json.

PR: feature/revenue-report — Security preliminary review completed and forwarding for architecture review. Summary of findings and action items for ArchReviewer to validate before merge/deploy:

payload:
Responsible-AI review summary & required mitigations (actionable confirmations and blockers):

1) ACLs & token scopes
- Confirmed concerns: requirement for role-based enforcement (finance/admin) across API gateway, microservices and background jobs is necessary. Must verify end-to-end enforcement (gateway -> service -> downstream) and that delegated tokens cannot escalate privileges.
- Required mitigations before Arch can be approved: enforce scoped JWT/OAuth tokens with audience and scope checks at gateway and at each service boundary; use token introspection or mTLS between services; ban long-lived delegated tokens or implement token-exchange with limited scope; ensure background jobs run under dedicated least-privilege service accounts and audit those actions. Add automated tests that assert scope validation and negative tests that attempt scope elevation.

2) Input validation & attack surface
- Confirmed concerns: server-side validation must be authoritative. Model/analytics ingest points are potential poisoning vectors.
- Required mitigations: implement strict JSON schema validation (reject additionalProperties), canonicalize inputs (normalize timezones to UTC), enforce numeric bounds (no negative/overflow amounts), enforce max lengths, content-type checks, and defensive parsing to avoid injection. Validate/whitelist fields used by downstream analytics/ML; add anomaly detectors for unusual data patterns. Add fuzz tests and CI validation for edge cases.

3) Rate-limiting, caching & scaling
- Confirmed concerns: expensive report generation and DoS risks.
- Required mitigations: enforce API gateway/WAF rate limits (per-user, per-tenant, and global), leaky-bucket or token-bucket policies with burst controls. For heavy reports: implement async job queue with controlled concurrency, pagination/streaming for large results, cache idempotent report results (ETags, time-to-live) and add cache invalidation strategy. Add circuit-breakers around downstream services, backpressure in workers, request-cost metering (per-request estimated cost) and autoscaling policies tied to queue depth and latency. Include quota enforcement and graceful degradation paths.

4) Logging, monitoring & privacy (data residency)
- Confirmed concerns: PII leakage and residency/compliance.
- Required mitigations: do not log PII in plaintext; adopt field-level redaction or irreversible hashing/salting for identifiers used in logs; structured logs with role-based ACL to access logs; redact or mask in dashboards. Define retention policies and archive/expire logs per compliance. Ensure encryption at rest/in-transit and geo-fencing for tenant data; document data flows and prove storage locations meet regulatory requirements. Add SLOs/alerts for high-latency, high-error rates, and model-drift/model-telemetry anomalies.

5) DB migration & backfill rollout
- Confirmed concerns: risk of downtime, replica lag, locks.
- Required mitigations: zero-downtime migration pattern: deploy DB changes as additive (nullable columns), deploy app tolerant of both schemas (dual-write/dual-read if needed), run incremental backfills in small batches off-peak, monitor replica lag and locks, use non-blocking operations and throttled workers. Provide tested rollback scripts and a runbook with metrics to abort/resume. Validate on staging with production-sized data.

6) Secrets & CI
- Confirmed concerns: secrets leakage and over-privileged CI roles.
- Required mitigations: store secrets in centralized vault/secret manager with ACLs and rotation; do not print secrets to logs or artifacts; use ephemeral short-lived credentials for CI and least-privilege scopes for CI/CD service accounts; scan pipelines for secrets exposure and add pipeline policy to block secrets in code or artifacts.

7) Responsible-AI specific checks
- Confirmed concerns: re-identification, aggregation thresholds, bias and regulatory risk for analytics/ML consuming this data.
- Required mitigations: assess re-identification risk for any exported/aggregated datasets; enforce minimum aggregation thresholds (k-anonymity or minimum cohort sizes) and consider differential-privacy mechanisms for analytics outputs; log and monitor feature usage and drift; run pre-deployment bias/fairness evaluation for any model trained or updated with this data and require human review for policy-sensitive decisions. Maintain documentation and decision-logs for model changes for audit.

Blocking items (must be addressed before Arch sends back to SecurityReviewer):
- Proof that token scope enforcement is implemented and tested end-to-end (gateway + services + background jobs) with no privilege escalation path.
- Server-side strict validation implemented (schemas, reject extra fields) and CI tests for edge cases.
- Plan for handling expensive reports (async job + rate-limits + cache) with circuit-breaker/backpressure and per-tenant quotas.
- Logging/privacy controls and data residency mapping with retention policy documented.
- Migration/backfill runbook and tested rollback procedures.
- Secret management in vault and CI least-privilege demonstration.
- Responsible-AI mitigations for analytics (aggregation thresholds/differential privacy) and a fairness/bias review process for model updates.

If the above are implemented or have concrete, testable plans and runbooks attached, Responsible-AI can approve and I will forward final OK. If any of these are missing, Merger should request an 'Again' cycle to ArchReviewer with clear remediation items.

1) End-to-end token scope enforcement (API gateway → services → background jobs)
- Implementation: gateway token-exchange per RFC8693 (auth/token_exchange.py), delegated short-lived tokens (TTL=60s) minted with minimal scopes, service middleware enforces scopes (auth/middleware.py), background-worker validates job-scoped metadata before job execution (worker/auth_job_guard.py).
- mTLS & introspection: token-introspection service with mTLS between services (auth/introspect/, certs mocked for CI). Details and cert rotation in runbooks/token_scope_runbook.md.
- Tests & proof: automated positive & negative tests (tests/auth/test_scope_propagation.py, tests/auth/test_negative_privilege_escalation.py). CI job: ci/jobs/auth_contract_check.yml — artifacts/logs/auth_scope_test_run.txt and junit XML attached (artifacts/auth_scope_tests/ run_id: 2026-07-30-1234). Recorded test trace demonstrating attempted escalation rejected (artifacts/auth_scope_tests/negative_trace.log).

2) Server-side strict input validation & canonicalization
- Schemas: schemas/revenue_request.schema.json (additionalProperties:false, maxLength constraints, numeric bounds, timestamp format strict RFC3339UTC). Timezone canonicalization middleware (utils/time/canonicalize.py) forces UTC and rejects ambiguous timezone strings.
- Defensive parsing & content-type: API returns 415 for non-application/json; strict parser options enabled (api/config/strict_json=true).
- Tests & proof: unit tests (tests/validation/test_schema_rejects_additional_props.py), fuzz harness (tests/validation/fuzz_revenue_payloads.py) with CI job ci/jobs/fuzz_validation.yml — fuzz report attached (artifacts/fuzz/rev3_fuzz_report.json). Timezone canonicalization tests (tests/validation/test_timezone_canonicalization.py) and their CI artifact (artifacts/validation/tz_tests_junit.xml).

3) Expensive-report handling (queue, quotas, caching, backpressure)
- Design & config: runbooks/report_queue_design.md — controlled concurrency worker pools, idempotency keys, request-cost metering (meter/report_costs.py), per-tenant quota rules (config/quotas/tenant_quota.yaml).
- Autoscaling tied to queue depth: k8s HPA manifest deployments/hpa/report-worker-hpa.yaml and autoscaler test harness (tests/devops/test_hpa_queue_depth_scaling.py). Autoscale test run artifacts: artifacts/devops/hpa_scaling_run_2026-07-29.log.
- Caching/ETags & invalidation: services/cache/invalidate.py, object-store ETag behavior unit tests (tests/cache/test_etag_invalidation.py).
- Circuit-breaker/backpressure & rate limits: services/circuit_breaker.py and gateway rate-limiter config (config/rate_limits/global.yaml). Integration load tests (ci/jobs/load_tests/report_rate_limit.yml) produced attached load test report (artifacts/load/rev3_load_report.html) showing backpressure + Retry-After behavior under overload.
- Pagination/streaming: api/reports/streaming.py and tests (tests/reports/test_streaming_pagination.py).

4) Logging/privacy & data residency (proofs)
- Field-level PII redaction/hashing: logging/scrubber.py applied before emission; tests: tests/logging/test_redaction.py (artifact: artifacts/logs/redaction_test_output.log).
- RBAC for logs/dashboards: docs/log_access_controls.md and attached proof screenshots/ACL configs (docs/data_residency_proof/log_acl_screenshot.png).
- Encryption & retention: docs/log_retention_policy.md plus storage encryption proof (docs/data_residency_proof/s3_bucket_policy_and_region.txt). All proofs attached under docs/data_residency_proof/.

5) DB migration/backfill runbook & tested rollback
- Migration artifacts: migrations/2026xxxx_revenue_fields.sql and backfill tool tools/backfill/backfill_tool.py with throttling/resume support.
- Runbook: runbooks/db_migration_runbook.md — zero-downtime additive plan, dual-write option, replica-lag thresholds, lock monitoring scripts (tools/backfill/monitor_replica_lag.py), rollback script tools/backfill/rollback.sh.
- Staging validation: executed migration/backfill on staging with production-sized sample (dataset: staging-prod-sample-1TB). Preflight & postflight validation CI job ci/jobs/migration_preflight.yml produced artifacts (artifacts/migration/preflight_2026-07-28.tar.gz) including validation query results and timing metrics.

6) Secrets & CI (vault + scanning)
- Central vault integration: auth/vault_integration.md (Vault policies, rotation cadence, ACLs). CI uses OIDC ephemeral creds; no secrets stored in repo.
- Secret-scan: ci/jobs/secret_scan.yml produced artifact artifacts/secret_scan_report.json (run_id: 2026-07-30-0900) — no findings.
- Runbook for rotation: runbooks/secret_rotation.md.

7) Responsible-AI mitigations (re-identification, DP, fairness, decision-logs)
- Re-identification assessment: scripts/ai/reid_assessment.py executed; report attached artifacts/reid_report.pdf with risk scores and mitigation actions.
- Aggregation thresholds & DP: ai/dp/implementation.py enforces configurable min_cohort_size and optional Laplace noise; tests (tests/ai/test_dp_enforcement.py) and CI job ci/jobs/responsible_ai_check.yml produced artifact artifacts/ai/dp_test_results.json.
- Fairness/bias review: scripts/ai/fairness_eval.py, sample report artifacts/fairness_report_sample.pdf, and documented review flow runbooks/responsible_ai_runbook.md. Decision-logs stored in ai/decision_logs/ with access controls and retention policies detailed in runbook.

   - Prove token-introspection responses are not cached insecurely anywhere (show config/TTL on caches or evidence that introspection uses mTLS per-call or safe caching policy).

2) Scope-propagation negative-test coverage
   - Provide coverage metrics and logs for negative tests that attempt scope escalation across gateway→service→worker paths (show failing test logs and evidence that worker processes reject elevated-scope tokens).

   - Demonstrate that schema rejection is enforced centrally at the gateway and again at services (show gateway reject logs + service-side rejection tests).
   - Provide tests for content-type/charset attacks (e.g., "text/plain; charset=UTF-7"/multipart trickery) and duplicate/nested-field canonicalization cases (Unicode normalization, repeated keys) proving consistent canonicalization to UTC for timestamps.

4) Noisy-tenant isolation & autoscale safety
   - Provide tenant-isolation design: either per-tenant queues or strict weighted quotas; include config for per-tenant limits and how noisy tenants are throttled.
   - Provide safe autoscale parameters (scale rate, cooldown, max replicas, scale-down policy) and runbook for emergency scale-in/scale-out thresholds. Include a flood-test report demonstrating graceful degradation under noisy-tenant flood.

   - Provide concrete replica-lag thresholds, batch sizing guidance used in the attached backfill scripts, monitoring dashboards/alerts for replica lag/locks, and explicit abort/rollback triggers with tested behavior logs from a staging run.

8) DP/noise parameters and query-auditing

If DP not used for certain endpoints, provide rationale and stronger aggregation thresholds or min-cohort sizes.

Attached evidence (paths relative to PR): artifacts/auth_scope_tests/{revocation_timing_trace_v2.log,revocation_regression_results_v2.json,introspection_percall_mtls_proof.txt}, config/auth/introspection_cache.yaml, auth/{token_exchange.py,worker_token_exchange.py,introspect/}, tests/auth/test_replay_and_revocation_regression.py; worker/auth_job_guard.py, tests/analytics/test_ingest_scope_negative.py, artifacts/services/rejections/analytics_worker_rejects_sanitized.log; schemas/revenue_request.schema.json, utils/time/canonicalize.py, artifacts/validation/{normalization_and_rejection_junit.xml,fuzz/content_type_charset_attack_run_v2.json}; config/queue/tenancy/, config/quotas/tenant_quota.yaml, deployments/hpa/report-worker-hpa.yaml, artifacts/devops/noisy_tenant_flood_test.pdf, artifacts/load/rev8_tenant_flood_test.html; migrations/2026xxxx_revenue_fields.sql, tools/backfill/*, runbooks/db_migration_runbook.md, artifacts/migration/{preflight_2026-07-28.tar.gz,replica_lag_run.log,rollback_test_output.txt}; auth/vault_integration.md, runbooks/secret_rotation.md, artifacts/ci/{ci_role_matrix.csv,vault_acl_snapshot.json,vault_rotation_report.txt,secret_scan_report.json}; logging/scrubber.py, artifacts/logs/{sanitized_sample_logs.log,dlp_scan_report.json,log_acl_audit_record.json}, docs/data_residency_proof/; ai/dp/{dp_config.yaml,privacy_budget_manager.py,privacy_budget_enforcement.log,analytics_query_audit.log,dp_parameter_justification.txt).

Priority validation requested — please respond per-item with either APPROVE or list concrete issues (with failing artifact refs) and required remediation/tests, and state overall architecture approval status for Security final sign-off:
1) Token-exchange & introspection: validate RFC8693 flow (per-job short-lived worker tokens), token-replay protections, revocation propagation (<2s observed), and that introspection cache (<=1s/no-cache for sensitive scopes) and per-call mTLS cannot be abused. Attach any failing traces.
2) Rate-limiting/backpressure/quota design: validate per-tenant isolation, weighted quotas/per-tenant queues, quota enforcement under noisy-tenant flood tests, circuit-breaker behavior, request-cost metering, and HPA safety (scale-up/down rates, stabilization windows, blast-radius). See noisy_tenant_flood_test.pdf and rev8_tenant_flood_test.html for test outputs.
3) DB migration/backfill runbook: sign off zero-downtime strategy (dual-write/backfill), replica-lag abort thresholds, batching limits, and rollback triggers; flag any raw-SQL locking risks in migrations/2026xxxx_revenue_fields.sql or preflight logs.
4) Logging/data-residency: confirm PII redaction/scrubbing effectiveness, DLP scan results, log ACL enforcement, retention/replication region mapping compliance (docs/data_residency_proof/), and confirm analytics logs are not replicated to non-compliant regions.
5) Responsible-AI / DP: validate DP epsilon/delta choices, privacy-budget manager behavior under concurrent queries, aggregation thresholds, and protections against re-identification via correlated queries; cite privacy_budget_enforcement.log or analytics_query_audit.log for issues.

Requested deliverable: per-priority-item explicit APPROVE or list of concrete issues (with artifact refs) and remediation/tests required, plus final overall architecture approval decision for Security to complete final sign-off.
